This operation allows a new administrator to register with their email and password. When a request is received, the system validates the email format and ensures the password meets complexity requirements (minimum 12 characters, one number, one special character). The password is securely hashed with bcrypt before storage. The administrator record is created in the economic_discussion_administrators table with default values for display name and bio. An entry is created in the economic_discussion_administrator_sessions table to track the session. The system then generates a JWT access token valid for 15 minutes and a refresh token valid for 7 days. Both tokens are returned in the response body with the IAuthorized structure. This operation is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

Security considerations require hashing passwords with bcrypt to prevent exposure of plaintext credentials. The use of short-lived access tokens reduces risk from token compromise, while the refresh token enables token renewal without requiring re-authentication. Session tracking in administrator_sessions enables future audit trails and potential session invalidation if needed.

The administrator actor has higher privileges than citizens, so registration is designed to be restricted to verified administrative users. This operation does not support pre-existing accounts - only new administrators can be registered. This prevents unauthorized access escalation.

Related operations include login, refresh, and password reset. After successful join, users may proceed to login for subsequent sessions. The token response format is consistent with other authentication operations for unified client handling.

operations.description:
This operation authenticates an administrator by validating their email and password against the stored bcrypt hash in the economic_discussion_administrators table. Upon receiving a login request, the system locates the user record by email address and compares the provided password against the stored hash using bcrypt verification. If the hash matches, the system creates a new entry in the economic_discussion_administrator_sessions table to log the active session and generates a JWT access token valid for 15 minutes and a refresh token valid for 7 days. Both tokens are returned in the response body using the IAuthorized structure. This operation is publicly accessible and does not require prior authentication.

If the credentials do not match or the user account does not exist, the system returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized with the AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS error code. This prevents user enumeration by providing the same response for non-existent accounts and invalid passwords.

The system leverages the existing administrator password storage in the economic_discussion_administrators table. Password reset functionality is handled separately through password_reset_tokens in economic_discussion_administrator_password_resets table, and should not be used for authentication logic here.

The token format follows the IAuthorized schema consistently across all authentication operations, ensuring client-side consistency. The access token contains the actor type, user ID, and expiration time, signed with a secure secret key. The refresh token is a cryptographically random string stored in the database with expiry and revocation tracking.

Related operations include join, refresh, and password reset. After successful login, the administrator may use the refresh token to obtain new access tokens without re-authenticating. The system does not support logout as a server-side operation - clients discard tokens upon logout.

This operation must not be used to authenticate citizen accounts - only administrator accounts may use this endpoint.

operations.description:
This operation allows an administrator to obtain a new access token using a valid refresh token, extending their session without re-authenticating with credentials. The system receives the refresh token and checks its validity against active session records in the economic_discussion_administrator_sessions table. If the refresh token is found, hasn't expired, and hasn't been revoked, the system generates a new JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a new refresh token (valid for 7 days). The old refresh token is marked as expired and the new one is stored in the session record. The new access token and refresh token are returned in the response body using the IAuthorized structure.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found in the session records, the system returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized with AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID error code. This prevents token replay attacks and ensures that compromised tokens cannot be reused.

The system tracks refresh token states in administrator_sessions to support revocation and audit. Revoked tokens will be rejected even if they are cryptographically valid. This mechanism balances convenience of token renewal with security of token lifecycle control.

This operation is publicly accessible to any client presenting a valid refresh token, as it does not require the user's password. The refresh token must be securely stored client-side, separate from the access token.

Related operations include login and join. This operation is the only mechanism to renew an authenticated session after the access token expires. The system does not support logout as a server-side operation - clients discard tokens upon logout.

No email verification or 2FA mechanisms are involved in this flow, as the database lacks fields for these features.

Sections are pre-populated with "Politics", "Economy", and "Current Affairs" during system initialization and can be created or modified by administrators, but all authenticated users can access this full list of available sections for browsing. The operation returns exactly 20 sections per page, with the ability to navigate through the complete collection using pagination controls.

The list is ordered alphabetically by section name to ensure consistent and predictable user experience, enabling users to quickly locate specific sections. This operation does not require any request parameters for filtering or search, as the requirement specifies retrieval of all sections without restrictions.

Security: Accessible to all authenticated users regardless of role (citizen or administrator). Admins have additional capabilities to create, edit, or delete sections, but this endpoint only provides read access to the section list.

Performance: The section list is expected to be small (typically under 20 items), so pagination is implemented for architectural consistency with other list endpoints rather than performance necessity. Results are cached for 5 minutes to optimize load times for frequent access.

The section name is a required field with a length between 3 and 50 characters, while the description is required and must be between 50 and 500 characters. Include associated article tags from economic_discussion_article_tags junction table in the response. Include comment count by joining with economic_discussion_comments and counting rows. Cache results for 2 minutes with cache key based on sectionId and pagination parameters.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of articles that belong to a specific section in the economic discussion platform.

This operation performs a filtered search of articles within a designated section, returning a summary view optimized for display in list interfaces. It queries the economic_discussion_articles table directly, using the sectionId path parameter to filter records by the section_id foreign key, thereby identifying all articles associated with the targeted section.

The response includes essential information for article listings: article title, author identifier, associated tags, total comment count, and timestamp of creation. The full article content is not included in this summary as required by the business specifications, ensuring optimized response sizes and efficient client-side rendering. Each article in the response represents an entry in the article listing for the chosen section.

Security and authorization: Only authenticated users may perform this search. Users without access to the section (e.g., banned or unauthorized) receive an empty result set or error as appropriate. Rate limiting applies to prevent excessive querying. This operation is read-only, with no data manipulation permitted.

Related operations: GET /sections/{sectionId} retrieves section metadata; POST /sections/{sectionId}/articles creates new articles in the section; GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves the full content of an individual article.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of article summary information for articles within the specified section.

operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_comments table filtered by article_id field, ordered by created_at in ascending order (oldest first). Apply pagination with 20 comments per page using cursor-based pagination for efficiency. Include only comment content, author_id, and created_at fields in result. Exclude any deleted comments (if soft-delete flag exists, filter by it; but schema shows no such field). Cache results for 1 minute using caching key built from articleId and pagination cursor.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of comments associated with a specific article.

This operation returns all comments made on a particular article, sorted from oldest to newest to maintain chronological conversation flow. Comments are displayed with their content, creation timestamp, and author identification, enabling users to follow the discussion thread in sequence.

The system retrieves only comments that are actively visible, with no soft-delete mechanism in place as specified in the requirements. The results are limited to 20 comments per page to ensure optimal performance, particularly when an article receives high volumes of comments. Users can navigate through pages to view the complete comment history.

Comment visibility is restricted to comments linked to the requested article; no cross-article comment filtering occurs. This endpoint is accessible to all authenticated users (citizens and administrators). The article's existence is enforced by the path parameter, and any attempt to access comments for a non-existent article returns a 404 error.

For performance, the system serves this content from cache when possible, significantly reducing database load for popular articles. The implementation follows the business requirements that comments should be displayed in chronological order without nested replies and with full visibility of all posted comments. This endpoint is read-only; comments can be created or modified via separate POST and PUT operations.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target article whose comments are being retrieved (UUID format)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of comment summaries for the specified article

operations.description:
Create a new comment on a specified article in the economic/political discussion board. This operation allows authenticated users to submit textual comments that are associated with a specific article identified by the articleId path parameter. The comment content must be between 1 and 5,000 characters and cannot be empty.

The comment is linked to the authenticated user who is making the request. The system enforces that the user must be authenticated and not banned to submit a comment. The comment creation triggers an automatic update to the article's comment count, which is maintained as a denormalized field for performance optimization.

When a comment is created, the system records the current timestamp in Asia/Seoul timezone and stores the comment in the economic_discussion_comments table. The comment is permanently inserted and cannot be reverted — deletion performs a hard delete, removing the record entirely from the database.

This operation supports the core discussion functionality of the platform, allowing users to engage with content through direct textual responses. The operation ensures data integrity by validating content length requirements and authenticating all requestors.

Related operations: GET /economicDiscussion/citizen/articles/{articleId}/comments (retrieve comments), PUT /economicDiscussion/citizen/comments/{commentId} (edit comment), DELETE /economicDiscussion/citizen/comments/{commentId} (delete comment).
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Validate that user is authenticated and not banned. Extract authenticated user ID from JWT. Verify article exists and is active. Validate comment content length between 1-5000 characters. Reject if empty or exceeds limit. Generate new unique comment ID. Insert comment with article_id from path, author_id from JWT, content from request body, created_at and updated_at set to current Asia/Seoul time, and status='active'. Increment article's comment_count field by 1. Return created comment object with all fields including generated ID, timestamps, and status.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to which the comment should be added.
parameters.name: articleId

requestBody.description: The content of the new comment. Must contain at least 1 character and no more than 5,000 characters.

responseBody.description: The newly created comment object with all its properties including system-generated fields like ID, timestamps, and associated article ID.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single comment by its unique identifier from the economic_discussion_comments table. This operation is used when a user views an article and wants to see the details of a specific comment within the comment thread. The comment data includes the full content, its creation timestamp, and reference to the article it belongs to, but does not include any nested data about the article or the author.

Security considerations are enforced at the API gateway level based on user roles, but since comment display is public-facing on article pages, this operation is accessible to both authenticated and unauthenticated users. The comment is permanently removed from the database when deleted by its author, and will return a 404 error if queried after deletion.

The operation maps directly to the economic_discussion_comments table schema as defined in the database, with fields including id, content, created_at, article_id, and author_id. The comment's content is displayed exactly as stored in the database, with no formatting restrictions or truncation applied, allowing users to see the full text as originally submitted.

This operation supports the system's requirement to display comments on article pages. When a user clicks on a comment or views comments in a thread, this endpoint is called to retrieve the full comment details. It works in tandem with the architecture's requirement to sort comments from oldest to newest by relying on the created_at field for chronological ordering in the application layer. No other API operations are required to be performed before this one, as comment data is stored independently and can be retrieved without referencing other entities.
operations.name: getByCommentid
operations.specification: Query the economic_discussion_comments table by the provided commentId parameter. Return the record with fields: id, content, created_at, article_id, author_id. If no matching record exists, return HTTP 404. Implement caching of comment data for 5 minutes using commentId as cache key. Ensure SQL query uses indexed lookup on id field. No transactions needed as this is a read-only operation.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the comment to retrieve.
parameters.name: commentId

responseBody.description: Complete comment record including all fields from the economic_discussion_comments table.

operations.specification: Update existing comment in database with validation. Query economic_discussion_comments table by commentId and verify user has permission to update (must match comment author_id). Update content field with validated input (5-1000 characters). Set updated_at to current timestamp. Return updated comment object with all fields. Validate comment exists before update. Return 404 if comment not found. Return 403 if user lacks permissions. Throw 400 if content length is outside 5-1000 character range.
operations.description:
Update an existing comment on an article in the Economic/Political Discussion Board.

This operation allows a user to modify the content of their own comment, replacing the entire text with new content. Comments are associated with articles and represent user contributions to discussions. Only the comment's content can be updated; the author, creation timestamp, and other metadata remain unchanged and cannot be modified through this API.

The operation requires the user to be authenticated and must match the original comment author. The comment content must be between 5 and 1,000 characters in length. Comments shorter than 5 characters or longer than 1,000 characters will be rejected. This length constraint ensures comments remain concise while allowing sufficient room for meaningful contributions.

When a comment is successfully updated, the system updates the timestamp to reflect when the change occurred, and returns the full updated comment object to the client. This allows the client to update its local state with the most current data, including the updated timestamp.

The operation does not affect other users' comments or any other data in the system. Comment edits are visible to all users who have access to the article, but no edit history is maintained - only the current state of the comment is preserved.

Related operations: create comment (POST /comments), list comments (PATCH /comments), delete comment (DELETE /comments).

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target comment to be updated

requestBody.description: The new content for the comment, replacing the existing content. Must be 5-1,000 characters in length.

responseBody.description: The full comment object after it has been successfully updated, including the new content and updated timestamp.

operations.specification: Delete the comment record from the economic_discussion_comments table by its primary key commentId. operations.description:
Permanently deletes a specific comment from the Economic/Political Discussion Board.

This operation removes a comment identified by its unique commentId from the economic_discussion_comments database table. All deleted comments are permanently erased from the system with no ability to recover, in accordance with the hard delete policy specified in the requirements.

Security note: Only the comment's author or an administrator with appropriate permissions may delete a comment. The system verifies the requesting actor's authorization based on token claims before executing the deletion.

This delete operation does not affect other entities. Comments are not nested or cascaded to other tables, so deletion only affects the single comment record. This aligns with the requirement that comments are single-level only and are not dependent on other comment records.

Related operations: View comment (GET /comments/{commentId}), Edit comment (PUT /comments/{commentId}).

parameters.name: commentId

operations.specification:
Update the status of an administrator request decision in the economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions table.

1. Fetch the decision record by decisionId from economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions.
2. Validate decision status is one of: 'approved', 'rejected'.
3. If status is 'approved', update the associated administrator_request record's status to 'approved' and trigger user role upgrade.
4. If status is 'rejected', update the associated administrator_request record's status to 'rejected'.
5. Log the decision timestamp and the super administrator's ID who made the decision.
6. If decision reason is provided, update the reason field in the decision record.
7. Return the updated decision record including all fields: id, request_id, status, reason, decided_by, decided_at.

Use database transaction to ensure atomicity of decision update and related administrator_request update.

Error handling:
- Return 404 if decisionId doesn't exist
- Return 400 if status is invalid
- Return 403 if user is not a super administrator
- Return 400 if decision already has a status assigned
operations.description:
Update the status of a pending administrator promotion request decision.

This operation allows super administrators to review and act on pending administrator promotion requests submitted by citizens. Super administrators can either approve or reject the request, which determines whether the requesting user will be promoted from citizen to administrator status.

When a super administrator approves a request, the system automatically upgrades the requesting citizen's role to administrator and grants all administrator privileges, including content moderation and section management capabilities. When a request is rejected, the citizen remains with standard user privileges and must wait for a future opportunity to reapply.

The decision record is permanently stored in the economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions table for audit purposes, ensuring complete traceability of all administrator promotion actions. This decision record includes the final status (approved/rejected), the super administrator ID who made the decision, and an optional reason for rejection.

Access to this endpoint is strictly limited to users with super administrator privileges. Regular administrators cannot use this endpoint to approve or reject requests, as this capability is reserved for the highest-level authority. The system enforces this access control through JWT token role validation.

This operation is part of the critical administrator promotion workflow that maintains system security and ensures only qualified users receive elevated permissions. All decisions are logged with timestamps and actor identification to prevent abuse and maintain accountability in the administrative hierarchy.

parameters.name: decisionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the administrator request decision record to update. This ID links to the economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions table.

requestBody.description: Update the status and optional reason for an administrator request decision.

responseBody.description: The complete administrator request decision record after update, including status, reason, and decision metadata.

operations.specification:
Query economic_discussion_administrator_requests table with cursor-based pagination for efficiency.
Apply filter on status field (only 'pending' status should be returned - this is the only state that needs review).
Optionally filter by submitted_at date range (from/to) if parameters provided.
Sort by submitted_at in ascending order (oldest first) to maintain chronological review order.
Return only essential fields: id, user_id, reason, submitted_at, status (avoid full content to optimize performance).
Cache results for 1 minute with cache key based on filter parameters.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of pending administrator request submissions awaiting review by super administrators.

This operation queries the administrator_requests table and provides advanced filtering capabilities specifically for super administrators reviewing pending requests. Only requests with status 'pending' are returned, as completed decisions (approved/rejected) do not require further review.

The operation supports filtering by submission date range to allow super administrators to focus on recent requests or review older submissions, though filters are optional. Results are sorted chronologically with oldest requests first to ensure fairness in review queue management.

This API interface is designed for the super administrator dashboard, where each request appears in a list with minimal necessary details: a preview of the request reason, submission timestamp, and status. Full request details, including the requesting user's profile data and any additional context, are available through separate endpoint calls.

Security considerations include strict role validation - only super administrators have access to this endpoint. Rate limiting applies to prevent abuse of the search functionality with excessive filtering parameters. The response is optimized for rapid display in the administrator user interface, prioritizing performance over comprehensive data retrieval.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and filtering parameters for administrator request review

responseBody.description: Paginated list of administrator request summaries for super administrator review

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_administrator_requests table by requestId. Return the complete administrator request record including requester_id, reason, status, submitted_at, and decision fields if available. Validate that requesting user has super administrator role. Return HTTP 404 if request not found. Return HTTP 403 if requesting user lacks super administrator privileges.
operations.description:
Retrieve a specific administrator privilege escalation request by its unique identifier. This operation allows super administrators to review individual administrator promotion requests submitted by citizens. The system uses this endpoint to retrieve the complete details of a pending administrator request for review and decision-making purposes.

The operation returns a specific administrator request identified by its unique requestId. This request contains the requester's identity, their submitted reason for seeking administrator privileges, the date and time the request was submitted, and currently established status. This data enables super administrators to evaluate the merit of each request before deciding to approve or reject it.

Security: Only super administrators can execute this operation. Citizens and regular administrators attempting to retrieve administrator requests will receive a 403 Forbidden response. The requester's identity is never exposed to non-administrative users, preserving privacy and security. The request reason text is provided in full for comprehensive review.

Related operations: PATCH /administrator-requests lists all pending administrator requests for bulk review, while PUT /administrator-requests/{requestId}/approve and PUT /administrator-requests/{requestId}/reject are used to approve or reject individual requests.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific administrator request to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete details of the administrator request including requester information, request reason, submission timestamp, and status

Query the economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions table using the request_id to locate the specific pending request. Validate that the requesting user has super administrator privileges. Update the decision_status field to either 'approved' or 'rejected' based on the incoming request body. Record the super administrator's ID who made the decision and the timestamp of the decision. If status is 'approved', update the corresponding citizen's role to 'administrator' in the economic_discussion_citizens table. If status is 'rejected', send a system notification to the citizen. Return the updated request decision record with current status and metadata.
operations.description:
Approve or reject a pending administrator request submitted by a citizen.

This operation allows super administrators to make final decisions on administrator promotion requests. Each request submitted by a citizen must be reviewed by a super administrator who can either approve or reject it. The operation requires a structured request body that includes the specific request identifier and the decision outcome (approved or rejected).

When a request is approved, the system automatically promotes the citizen to administrator status and notifies them of the decision. When a request is rejected, the system sends a notification to the citizen indicating their request was not approved. The decision record is permanently archived with the super administrator's identity and timestamp for audit purposes. This operation does not return a list of requests but rather updates a specific request record based on its unique identifier.

Only users with super administrator privileges can perform this action. Regular administrators cannot approve or reject requests.

This operation is critical to the administrator promotion workflow and ensures proper governance and accountability for privilege escalation in the system.

requestBody.description: Decision parameters for approving or rejecting an administrator request

responseBody.description: The updated administrator request decision record after processing

operations.name: patch

operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a new ban record in economic_discussion_bans table by linking the authenticated administrator's ID with the target user ID provided in the path parameter. Validate the ban reason from request body is between 10 and 500 characters. Store the ban reason, timestamp, administrator ID, and target user ID in the bans table. Do NOT change user status during this operation - the system will handle login denial during authentication based on bans presence. Return HTTP 204 No Content on successful creation.
operations.description:
Ban a user from the Economic/Political Discussion Board platform. This operation creates a permanent ban record associated with a specific target user, as defined by the user ID in the path.

Administrators must provide a reason for the ban, which must be between 10 and 500 characters, documenting the rationale for restricting the account. Once a user is banned, their access to the system is immediately revoked upon future login attempts. Importantly, their existing articles and comments remain visible on the platform to preserve content integrity. This is distinct from deletion, which permanently removes content.

The ban process is auditable: the reason provided, the administrator who imposed the ban, and the timestamp of the ban are permanently recorded in the database. These records are stored in the economic_discussion_bans table, which links the banned user ID to the administrator who issued the ban. The system does not send notification emails to banned users.

This operation complements the unban functionality (DELETE /bans/{userId}), which may be used if a ban is determined to be in error. The banning system is designed to enforce community guidelines while preserving valuable user-generated content for transparency.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of banned users with filtering and search capabilities. This operation queries the economic_discussion_bans table to return records of users who have been banned from the platform. The operation supports advanced filtering by username, ban reason, and ban date range to assist administrators in managing banned users.

Security considerations require that only authenticated administrators may access this endpoint. The ban reason field is only visible to administrators and is hidden from regular users. The operation returns only the minimum necessary information for ban management: user ID, username, ban reason, ban date, and the administrator who issued the ban.

This operation integrates with the economic_discussion_bans table as defined in the database schema and supports cursor-based pagination for optimal performance with large datasets. The request parameters allow administrators to focus their review on specific categories of banned users (e.g., recent bans, specific reasons like hate speech). Related operations include the ban processing endpoint (POST /bans) and the unban endpoint (DELETE /bans/{banId}).
operations.name: patch
operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_bans table with cursor-based pagination for efficiency. Join with economic_discussion_citizens to retrieve username for display. Filter by username (partial match), reason (partial match), and ban date range when provided. Apply sorting by ban date descending (newest first). Return pagination cursor with next link. Cache results for 1 minute with cache key based on pagination and filter parameters. Validate that user has administrator role before executing query.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering banned users

responseBody.description: Paginated list of banned user summaries matching search criteria

operations.description:
Record an administrative action to reinstate a user's access privileges to the Economic/Political Discussion Board system.

This operation logs an administrative unbanning event in the economic_discussion_unbans table, creating a permanent audit record that captures the administrator who performed the action and the timestamp of reinstatement. Upon unbanning, a previously banned user's access to the platform is restored, allowing them to log in, create content, and interact with other users.

Consistent with system requirements, this operation does not alter or delete any existing ban records in the economic_discussion_bans table. Both the original ban and subsequent unban are permanently maintained in the audit system to ensure full accountability and transparency of moderator actions.

All user-generated content (articles and comments) remains visible to other users, as specified in the requirements. The unbanning action affects only the user's access status, not their historical content. The system does not erase or modify previous ban records; instead, it creates a new, separate audit entry confirming the reinstatement.

Administrators may unban users at any time following the requirements workflow, and each action triggers an immutable audit record that cannot be modified or deleted. This architecture ensures complete traceability of all access control decisions on the platform.
operations.name: unban
operations.specification: Remove active ban record from economic_discussion_bans table based on user ID identified through administrative context. Log unbanning event in economic_discussion_unbans table with timestamp and administrator reference. Clear any cached bans for the user. Send system notification to the user about their reinstatement. Return success status without response body.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of users who have been unbanned from the platform.

This operation queries the economic_discussion_unbans table to identify users who were previously banned but have since been unbanned by administrators. Each record represents a successful reversal of a ban status.

The operation returns unified records that combine information from both the economic_discussion_bans and economic_discussion_unbans tables, showing the original ban reason and timestamp alongside the unbanning reason and timestamp.

Security: This endpoint is only accessible to users with administrator role, as it exposes sensitive moderation activity.

The results can be filtered by username, unbanning date range, or unbanning administrator. Results are paginated in groups of 20, supporting cursor-based navigation for large result sets.

This operation complements the ban management workflow by allowing administrators to audit unbanning decisions and review historical moderation patterns.

Related operations: GET /bans (lists currently banned users), PATCH /bans (bans a user)
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_unbans table joined with economic_discussion_bans and economic_discussion_citizens. Provide pagination with cursor-based scrolling for efficiency. Filter results by username (partial match), unbanning date (range), and unbanning admin (by ID). Order results by unbanned_at descending. Return fields: username, ban_reason, ban_timestamp, unbanning_reason, unbanned_at, unbanning_admin. Cache results for 5 minutes with parameters-based key. Ensure response includes pagination object with hasNext, hasPrevious, cursor, and limit.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination parameters for filtering unbanned users list.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summarized unbanned user records including original ban details and unbanning information.

operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a specific article from the Economic/Political Discussion Board system. This operation responds to the economic_discussion_articles database table and returns complete article information including title, content, author reference, section assignment, tags, and attached files. The article must be accessible to the authenticated user based on their permissions and the article's visibility status. This information is displayed to users when they view an individual article page.

Security considerations require that the system verify the user's authentication status and permissions before returning article data. If the article has been deleted (hard delete per requirements), the system must return HTTP 404 Not Found. No soft deletion is implemented, so articles in the database are always active and visible unless permanently removed.

This operation integrates with economic_discussion_articles to provide all article fields and with economic_discussion_article_tags to retrieve associated tags. File attachments are handled through economic_discussion_article_files, which stores metadata about all uploaded files including original filenames, sizes, and locations. The system supports PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PNG, JPG, JPEG, and GIF files up to 50MB each.

The article title is limited to 200 characters and may be truncated if longer, but the content may be up to 10,000 characters. Tags are free-text and comma-delimited, with up to 10 tags maximum per article. When the article was last edited, the updated_at timestamp reflects this change, while created_at maintains the original creation time.

Related operations: PATCH /articles for searching and filtering articles (index operation), DELETE /articles/{id} for deletion by the article's author (erase operation). The article listing (index operation) returns only summary information including title, author, tags, comment count, and time posted, while this operation returns the complete content for full viewing.
operations.name: getById
operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_articles table using the UUID provided in the path parameter. Join with economic_discussion_article_tags to retrieve all associated tags for this article. Join with economic_discussion_article_files to retrieve all attached file metadata. If article_id does not exist in database, return HTTP 404 Not Found. Apply caching strategy: cache results for 5 minutes with cache key based on article ID. Return full article record with all fields including author_id, created_at, updated_at, and attached files metadata. Validate UUID format before database query for performance optimization.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to retrieve in UUID format
parameters.name: id

responseBody.description: Complete article data including title, content, author reference, section association, tags, and all attached files

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific comment by its unique identifier from the economic_discussion_comments table.

This operation fetches the complete details of a single comment, including its content, creation timestamp, and associated author and article references. The comment is identified by its unique identifier which is stored as the primary key in the economic_discussion_comments database table.

Security considerations ensure that users can only retrieve comments that exist in the system, and the operation requires authentication to prevent anonymous access. The returned comment content is displayed exactly as stored in the database, preserving the original text format and any line breaks.

This operation complements the article viewing functionality, allowing users to access and review specific comments within an article's discussion thread. Related operations include listing all comments for an article (GET /articles/{id}/comments) and deleting a comment (DELETE /comments/{id}). For performance, the system caches comment details for up to 5 minutes.

Error handling includes returning HTTP 404 status code if the comment identifier does not exist in the database. This indicates either that the comment was deleted or never created, and the resource is not found.
operations.name: getById
operations.specification: Query the economic_discussion_comments table by id field to retrieve single comment record. Join with economic_discussion_citizens table to get author display name. Return comment content, creation timestamp, and author information. Include caching logic with 5-minute TTL using comment id as cache key. Validate that id is a valid UUID format before database query. Return HTTP 404 if comment not found. Do not return deleted comments (no soft delete in schema).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target comment in the database
parameters.name: id

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the specific comment identified by the provided ID.

operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query economic_discussion_comments table to retrieve all comments for a given article context. Filter comments by any specified tags using exact case-sensitive matching. Sort results by created_at timestamp in ascending order (oldest first). Retrieve full comment record with associated author display name from economic_discussion_citizens table. Do not implement pagination as requirements specify all comments load at once. Include only the comment content, author display name, and timestamps in the result set. Apply zero truncation or summarization - return complete comment data. Return 404 if no comments match the criteria (though no article context is in path, the UI context provides the article).
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered list of all comments associated with an article based on tag criteria. This operation retrieves the complete set of comments for a target article context (provided by the UI/client application) and applies optional tag-based filtering to narrow results. The result includes full comment content, the author's display name, the creation timestamp, and any other comment metadata as defined in the database schema.

Comments are always displayed in chronological order from oldest to newest, ensuring a natural conversation flow. The system does not implement pagination for comments due to expected low volume per article, so all matching comments are returned in a single response.

Tag filtering uses case-sensitive exact matching, meaning 'politics' and 'Politics' are treated as distinct tags. Users may select multiple tags to filter comments, and the system employs AND logic, returning only comments that contain ALL selected tags. This allows users to cross-reference comments based on multiple topics of interest.

The operation adheres to the database schema where the economic_discussion_comments table stores comment information with references to the citizen author and the article. The response includes dereferenced fields from the economic_discussion_citizens table to provide the author's display name directly in the comment object, eliminating the need for additional API calls to render comment authorship information.

This operation complements the GET /comments/{commentId} endpoint which retrieves a single comment by its unique identifier, but for listing multiple comments, this PATCH endpoint provides better performance and more flexible filtering.

requestBody.description: Search parameters for filtering comments by tags. This object includes the list of tags used to filter which comments are returned. Only comments containing all specified tags will be included in the results.

responseBody.description: List of comments matching the search criteria, with full details for display. Each comment includes the content, creation timestamp, author display name, and any associated metadata. No pagination is applied as the system returns all matching comments in a single response.

operations.description:
Update the current citizen's profile information including display name and bio.

This operation modifies the user profile associated with the authenticated citizen account. The request must include the complete profile object with both display_name and bio fields specified, as PUT operations replace the entire resource. operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics about tag usage across all articles in the Economic/Political Discussion Board system.

This operation provides administrators with analytics data about the frequency and recency of tag usage across all published articles. The system aggregates data from the economic_discussion_article_tags table which records the association between articles and the free-form text tags assigned to them. For each unique tag, this endpoint returns the total number of articles it has been used in and the timestamp of the most recent article where it was used.

The operation is designed to support administrative analysis of content trends, topic popularity, and community engagement patterns. Administrators can identify emerging topics, detect stale or abandoned tags, and assess the effectiveness of the tagging system in organizing content. The statistics data is critical for maintaining a well-organized content ecosystem and helping administrators make informed moderation decisions.

The endpoint supports paginated results with configurable page sizes to handle systems with thousands of unique tags. The data is computed on-demand from the article_tags table and returned in descending order of usage count, with the most popular tags appearing first. This design allows administrators to quickly identify high-impact tags without needing to scan through the entire dataset.

This operation should be used in conjunction with the tag filtering functionality on the article search page to understand how tags contribute to content discovery. Unlike the search endpoint which filters articles by tags, this endpoint provides meta-level statistics about the tags themselves.

Administrators can use this data to: identify trending topics for featured content promotion, prune rarely-used tags to maintain tagging system discipline, and recognize topics that could benefit from standardized tag creation to improve consistency.

Related operations: PATCH /articles with tag filtering, GET /articles with tag search, DELETE /article_tags to remove unused tags manually.

This operation enables super administrators to review and act upon administrator promotion requests. The system collects request submissions from citizens through a formal application process, and this endpoint exposes those pending requests for administrative review.

Relevant database table: economic_discussion_administrator_requests. This table stores all administrator requests with fields including requester_id, reason, created_at, and status. The status field determines whether a request is pending, approved, or rejected. This endpoint filters for only those records where status is "pending".

Security: This operation is restricted to super administrators only. Ordinary administrators and citizen users have no access to this endpoint. Authorization is enforced by the Endpoint agent.

This endpoint is used in conjunction with the POST /administrator-requests endpoint (where citizens submit requests) and the PATCH /administrator-requests/{requestId}/approve and PATCH /administrator-requests/{requestId}/reject endpoints (where super administrators act on requests). This endpoint is specifically for the "pending" status views in the administrative dashboard.

The operation returns a paginated response with 20 requests per page, sorted by creation time (newest first), and includes relevant details such as the requester's username, request reason, and submission timestamp.

The system does not implement soft deletion for administrator requests - requests are permanently marked as approved or rejected when processed.

The request contains a mandatory reason field with a minimum of 10 characters, which is used for audit purposes. Only users with super administrator privileges can perform this approval action. The approval triggers the user role update and sends a notification to the requesting user.

The operation logs the approval event with the super administrator's ID and timestamp for complete audit trail purposes. This operation does not delete the request record but marks it as approved for historical reference.

Related operations: PATCH /administrator-requests/reject (to deny a request), DELETE /administrator-requests/{requestId} (to cancel a pending request), and PATCH /administrator-requests (to view pending requests).

Users cannot cancel or appeal rejections themselves - the only path forward for a rejected candidate is to submit a new request after 30 days. Rejection reasons are visible to super administrators for oversight and are not shown to the requesting citizen, preserving the administrative discretion.

The rejection action permanently marks the request as rejected and prevents the citizen from receiving automatic notification of the reason, maintaining the integrity of the administrative decision-making process. The rejection is recorded with the rejecting super administrator's ID and timestamp for complete audit trails.

This operation does not affect the requester's account status, which remains as 'citizen'. It only updates the administrator request record in the system. The articles array is populated by querying articles where author_id equals the authenticated user's ID (from JWT). The comments array is populated by querying comments where author_id equals the authenticated user's ID. The tags property for each article is populated by joining with economic_discussion_article_tags and aggregating the tag values. The comment_count for each article is calculated via COUNT of related comments. All timestamps are in UTC format. The entire profile is cached for 3 minutes using the user_id as cache key.

IEconomicDiscussionArticleTag.description:
Represents a single tag's analytics summary from the Economic/Political Discussion Board system. Each object contains the tag name, the total number of articles where this tag has been used, and the timestamp of the most recent article where this tag was applied.

This type is used exclusively in administrative analytics endpoints to help moderators and administrators understand tag usage trends, identify popular and emerging topics, and detect stale or obsolete tags. Administrative staff can use these summaries to determine which tags should be promoted, standardized, or retired to improve content discoverability and community organization.

The tag name is displayed in full text, the usage count provides quantitative insight into topic popularity, and the last_used timestamp indicates the recency of the tag's activity, helping administrators prioritize recent trends over outdated ones.

Computed summary type for tag analytics. Sources: economic_discussion_article_tags table. Computed via: GROUP BY tag column. Requirements: Count the number of records per tag (TAG_COUNT), get the maximum created_at timestamp per tag (LAST_USED). Must exclude empty or null tags (filter WHERE tag IS NOT NULL AND tag != '').

This aggregate is not persisted in database but computed on-demand via SQL query: SELECT tag, COUNT(*) AS count, MAX(created_at) AS lastUsed FROM economic_discussion_article_tags WHERE tag IS NOT NULL AND tag != '' GROUP BY tag ORDER BY lastUsed DESC.

The calculation is performed for administrative analytics endpoints only, returning paginated summaries used for UI displays of tag popularity and recency.
